title: Composition of essentially smooth ring maps
statement: Let $R\to A$ and $A\to B$ be essentially smooth homomorphisms of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map]. Then the composite $R\to B$ is essentially smooth.

source.place: Used without statement in Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo) and the proof of Lemma Tag 07FJ, item (item-choose-deltai) (lines 2752-2830: D -> D' is enlarged repeatedly by Lemma 07FI, which needs the composite k[y]_p/p^n -> D' essentially smooth); statement and proof written by an agent (descend the smooth A-algebra to a smooth algebra over a principal localization of the smooth R-algebra of which A is a localization, by Algebra, Lemma Tag 0CAQ (lemma-smooth-descends-through-colimit), then compose smooth maps and localize)

proof.text: *The presentations.* By [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map] there are a smooth $R$-algebra $P$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], a multiplicative subset $S\subseteq P$ and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $A\cong S^{-1}P$; and a smooth $A$-algebra $Q$, a multiplicative subset $T\subseteq Q$ and an isomorphism of $A$-algebras $B\cong T^{-1}Q$. Since essential smoothness depends only on the isomorphism class of the algebra (step 1 of [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map]) we may replace $A$ by $S^{-1}P$ (transporting $Q$, $T$ and the structure maps along the isomorphism) and $B$ by $T^{-1}Q$; an isomorphism of $A$-algebras is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras for the structures through $R\to A$. So $R\to A=S^{-1}P$ is $R\to P\to S^{-1}P$, and $R\to B$ is $R\to S^{-1}P\to Q\to T^{-1}Q$. It suffices to find a smooth $R$-algebra $Q_0$, a multiplicative subset $U\subseteq Q_0$ and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $T^{-1}Q\cong U^{-1}Q_0$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Section 07FF (section-inseparable), uses of 'essentially smooth' in Lemma 07FI (line 2638) and the proof of Lemma 07FJ (line 2752); written by an agent

proof.text: *Descend $Q$ to a principal localization of $P$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-colimit-principal-localizations], $S$ preordered by divisibility is filtered and $A=S^{-1}P=\varinjlim_{f\in S}P_f$ in commutative rings, with coprojections $\kappa_f:P_f\to A$, $a/f^e\mapsto a/f^e$. Since $A\to Q$ is smooth, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-algebra-filtered-colimit-descent] gives an $s\in S$, a smooth ring map $\beta:P_s\to Q_0$ and an isomorphism of $A$-algebras $Q\cong A\otimes_{P_s}Q_0$, the tensor product formed via $\kappa_s$. Again transporting $T$, we may take $Q=A\otimes_{P_s}Q_0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00CR (lemma-localization-colimit, line 1243) and Lemma Tag 0CAQ (lemma-smooth-descends-through-colimit, line 38230)

proof.text: *$Q_0$ is smooth over $R$.* $R\to P$ is smooth and $s\in P$, so $R\to P\to P_s$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization]; $P_s\to Q_0$ is smooth (step 2); hence the composite $R\to P_s\to Q_0$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (2). We regard $Q_0$ as an $R$-algebra through this composite.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00T3 (lemma-localize-smooth, line 37113) and Lemma Tag 00TD (lemma-compose-smooth, line 37597), as recorded in the two cited Mathlib leaves

proof.text: *$Q$ is a localization of $Q_0$.* Let $\phi:P\to P_s$ and $\phi':P\to S^{-1}P$ be the localization maps. The powers of $s$ lie in $S$, and $\kappa_s\circ\phi=\phi'$ ([lem-weil-pbc-localization-colimit-principal-localizations], last clause), so by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] (2) (with $M=\{s^e\}\subseteq N=S$) $\kappa_s:P_s\to A$ is a localization of $P_s$ at the multiplicative subset $\phi(S)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] (with the ring $P_s$, the subset $\phi(S)$, $R'=A$ and $\psi=\beta:P_s\to Q_0$), $Q_0\to Q_0\otimes_{P_s}A$, $q\mapsto q\otimes1$, is a localization of $Q_0$ at $S_1=\beta(\phi(S))$; composing with the isomorphism $Q_0\otimes_{P_s}A\cong A\otimes_{P_s}Q_0=Q$, $q\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes q$ (conditions (a)-(c) of a localization are preserved by composing with a ring isomorphism), $\lambda:Q_0\to Q$, $q\mapsto1\otimes q$, is a localization of $Q_0$ at $S_1$. It is compatible with the $R$-structures: for $r\in R$ with image $p\in P$, $\lambda(\beta(\phi(p)))=1\otimes\beta(\phi(p))=\kappa_s(\phi(p))\otimes1=\phi'(p)\otimes1$, which is the image of $r$ under $R\to P\to S^{-1}P=A\to Q$.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00CM (section-localization) and Lemma Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization, line 2087), as recorded in lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change; written by an agent

proof.text: *$B$ is a localization of the smooth $R$-algebra $Q_0$; conclusion.* $\lambda:Q_0\to Q$ is a localization at $S_1$ (step 4) and $Q\to T^{-1}Q=B$ a localization at $T$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] (1) the composite $Q_0\to B$ is a localization of $Q_0$ at $U=\{x\in Q_0:\lambda(x)=t\lambda(\sigma)\text{ for some }t\in T,\ \sigma\in S_1\}$, and $B\cong U^{-1}Q_0$ as $Q_0$-algebras, hence as $R$-algebras, since the $R$-structure of $B$, $R\to A\to Q\to B$, equals $R\to Q_0\to Q\to B$ (step 4). As $Q_0$ is smooth over $R$ (step 3), $R\to B$ is essentially smooth [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map].
